From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: ACME — Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Tom/Priya — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the high-level cost levers we discussed so we can align on next steps. Please reply with anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- Token spend volatility during peak batch jobs (weekly ingestion spikes) driving unpredictable monthly bills.
- High per-token unit cost from current deployment and lack of batching/prefix caching.
- Latency SLOs for customer-facing features (~<250ms  p95) are non-negotiable.
- Procurement window: need a proposal for leadership by end of Q3; target budget ~USD 50k/month but flexible if ROI is clearly demonstrated.

Goals we heard:
1) Reduce monthly inference cost by at least 50% without regressions in latency or accuracy.
2) Provide a predictable monthly cost profile (smoothing / reserved options).
3) Validate token economics on a 30-day sample of production traffic.

High-level TCO levers and immediate observations (from today):
- Batching & continuous batching: grouping small requests into micro-batches can reduce per-token overhead on GPU serving; expected 10–25% unit cost improvement depending on request size distribution.
- Prefix/KV caching: for common prompts/conversations we can avoid re-computing prefixes and KV states — this can cut billed tokens and GPU work for conversational workloads (est. 5–20% savings on repetitive flows).
- Quantization & model selection: moving to an optimized quantized variant (if accuracy checks pass) reduces instance-level costs — may reduce per-instance cost by ~30–50%, trades: small accuracy delta to validate.
- Smart routing + reserved capacity: hybrid route (reserved Dedicated + burst Hosted) gives predictable base cost while enabling headroom for spikes.

Requested next steps (owners & timeline):
- Rafael: build a 3-scenario cost model (hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, private) using your 30-day sample + our batching/quantization assumptions. Deliverable: acme_tco_sheet_v1.xlsx. ETA: 2026-06-19.
- Naomi: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (infrastructure, KV cache integration, quantization constraints). ETA to schedule: 2026-06-17.
- Marissa (me): prepare an exec-friendly one-pager with 3-year ROI and procurement options. ETA: 2026-06-22.

Attachments: Rafael will attach an initial TCO spreadsheet and a pricing summary in follow-up. We also discussed you sharing a weekly usage export — Tom, if you can drop the CSV, Rafael will plug it into the model.

If that all looks right, I’ll queue Rafael and Naomi and we’ll target the follow-up deep-dive next week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Tom — thanks for the CSV, I’ll ingest that into the model this afternoon. Sharing a few technical assumptions so expectations are aligned: 

- Batching assumptions: we simulate micro-batching at 50–200 requests per batch depending on concurrency; for your request-size distribution from the CSV I’m seeing median tokens/request ~120 and a long tail. Expected batching uplift ~12–22% on unit cost.
- Prefix/KV caching: for conversational flows where the first ~30 tokens repeat across sessions, we model cache-hit rates of 15–30% depending on vertical. That maps to 5–15% reduction in billed compute for those flows.
- Quantization: we’ll model int8 and nf4-like quantized variants where applicable. Historically this reduces GPU memory and instance count allowing ~30–45% cost reduction at the instance layer; we’ll flag any potential accuracy regressions for your QA team to validate.
- Routing/Reserved capacity: committed Dedicated pools (monthly) reduce unit compute price but require a commit; we’ll show break-even horizon vs pure Hosted.

I attached draft artifacts: redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing bands and quantization notes) and acme_tco_sheet_v1.xlsx (input assumptions + scenario outputs). These are initial numbers — I’ll update after ingesting your CSV.

Next step: Rafael (me) -> update the spreadsheet and post a version with the specific batch/cache assumptions highlighted by 2026-06-19. Naomi -> please propose two time slots for the deep-dive.

—Rafael
